newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Siltek falls on Hewlett-Packard news.
newsitem.headline: Siltek falls on Hewlett-Packard news.

text.p: Shares in South African information technology group Siltek Ltd fell on Friday as market players digested the firm's move to sell some of its businesses and assets to U.S.-based Hewlett-Packard Co, dealers said.
By 1150 GMT Siltek shares were down 200 cents or 8.5 percent at 21.50 rand in moderate trade of 68,600 shares.
Some dealers said that the price Hewlett-Packard is expected to pay for the assets in Siltek's Hi-Performance Systems unit was not as high as had been anticipated.
"The market obviously pushed the share up expecting a certain price and they didn't get it, and that's why its coming off," a dealer said.
Siltek shares closed at a three month high of 23.50 rand ahead of the deal's announcement on Thursday. It has been on a steady upward run since May 19, broken for the first time on Friday.

Siltek and Hewlett-Packard Co said on Thursday they expected the purchase price, payable in cash on November 1, to be based on the tangible net asset value of the businesses as at October 31, plus a payment for goodwill.

"The proceeds of the disposal, including HiPerformance surplus cash retained by Siltek and commission on future sales, cannot be precisely quantified at this stage but is estimated to be of the order of 200 million rand," the firms said.
Other dealers said the sale announcement clouded Siltek's earnings potential.
"I will guess from this that it will look like Hi-Performance may be one of the stars in the Siltek group and maybe this news is not that good for Siltek's earnings," one said.
"Maybe the Hewlett-Packard story was positive initially but not now," he added.
